Calculation of Li/Li+ RedOx potential

The reliability of the method for assessing the potential of a negative charged electrode proposed in the "Results and Discussion" section was verified by the correspondence between the calculated and experimentally determined Li/Li+ Red/Ox potentials in an aqueous solution. The following half-reactions were used:
Hydrogen oxidation:
H2(aq) + 2nH2O(aq) -1ē → H2n+1On+(aq),								(S1)
Gºtheor, n →  = (937 ± 9) + (960 ± 80)·e-(1.1 ± 0.1)·n.
Eºtheor(ABS) = -Gºтеор/2F = -4.9 V.
Lithium oxidation:
Li-H2O(aq) + nH2O(aq) -1ē → H2O + Li+-nH2O(aq),						(S2)
Gºtheor, n →  = (111 ± 2) + (240 ± 2)·e-(0.52 ± 0.02)·n,
Eºtheor(ABS) = -Gºтеор/F = -1.15 V,
Eºtheor(SHE) = -1.15-(-4.9) = +3.75 V,
Li2-H2O(aq) + nH2O(aq) -1ē → Li-H2O + Li+-nH2O(aq),						(S3)
Gºtheor, n →  = (140 ± 2) + (240 ± 2)·e-(0.52 ± 0.02)·n,
Eºtheor(ABS) = -Gºтеор/F = -1.45 V,
Eºtheor(SHE) = -1.45-(-4.9) = +3.45 V,
Li6-H2O(aq) + nH2O(aq) -1ē → Li5-H2O + Li+-nH2O(aq),						(S4)
Gºtheor, n →  = (158 ± 2) + (240 ± 2)·e-(0.52 ± 0.02)·n,
Eºtheor(ABS) = -Gºтеор/F = -1.64 V,
Eºtheor(SHE) = -1.64-(-4.9) = +3.26 V,
where the notation (aq) with a subscript indicates that the solvent is additionally taken into account at the implicit approximation, n – number of water molecules delocalizing the positive charge. The proton solvation shell (n = 1 ÷ 4) was changed within the chosen functional/basis set and fixed solvation shell of the lithium ion (Table S2).

Table S2. Proton solvate complexes and equivalent water clusters within Li/Li+ Red/Ox potentials modelling.

The Gibbs free energy change of lithium oxidation in an aqueous solution with the most sophisticated model of negative charged electrode and infinite number of water molecules included in proton solvate complexes and equivalent water clusters is equal to -315 kJ·mol-1 and it corresponds +3.26 V (Eºexp = +3.040 V) according to quantum-chemical calculations.
